method: Site-specific HistGradientBoosting absolute-error ensembles predict demand and dwell time from local hour, weekday, charger limit and the optional last-request snapshot, using separate targets, two-seed averaging, recent-day weighting, request-value transforms and a charger-time demand cap. The public prediction interface adds a calibrated XGBoost ensemble for Caltech and JPL demand/dwell and a LightGBM ensemble for Caltech demand; these pairs improved time-ordered public holdout MAE. Office1 retains the stable predictor. To keep the previously calibrated world model and completion behavior unchanged, forecast and online dispatch call the stable V50-B predictor internally. Arrival rates use weekday-by-96-slot empirical frequencies; slots with mean arrivals below 0.30 use the daily-count median while busier slots retain the mean. The world model retains five joint ExtraTrees demand/dwell quantile cohorts for future arrivals and current vehicles, a bounded survival residual, and 64 complete historical-day particles for JPL and Office1. Natural load is the particle average, while capacity active count runs the same particle pool through earliest-deadline allocation under the public intervention capacity. Capacity_edf reports 50 percent of the particle EDF marginal effect. Caltech retains the validated v25 physical trajectory. Action planning uses half of the positive spread between the two demand-model seeds as a robust demand envelope, caps the optional request snapshot at 1.35 times that envelope, and applies a 1.25 completion margin. Deadline urgency uses a site-and-time empirical lower-dwell profile at 1.5 times its fifteenth percentile. No-slack vehicles are protected, and scarce capacity is concentrated on the smallest jobs. Office1 uses slack-first scheduling and shares residual power with tail-uncertainty vehicles.
assumptions: Only current-step observations are used for online actions.
Recent historical sessions are more representative of future behavior.
last_requested_energy_kwh is an optional snapshot and is never treated as a known final target.
Request uncertainty is bounded by the documented 1.35 demand-shift factor.
Demand, dwell and arrival assumptions stay unchanged when only counterfactual capacity changes.
Every charging interval is 0.25 hours and future charger capacity is 6.6 kW.
Historical arrivals are aggregate same-weekday counts aligned to the current quarter-hour step.
Current parked-vehicle count is available online and is predictive of future arrival intensity.
The empirical lower-dwell profile is an action-only deadline guard.
Historical-day particles are sampled only from training sessions available before the evaluation cutoff.
The public prediction blend is activated only for site-target pairs improved on public time holdouts.
limitations: Vehicle demand and departure time remain uncertain at arrival.
Office1 has sparse history, so its site-specific estimate is less stable.
capacity_edf represents a simulated physical response rather than real user behavior.
The Caltech natural-load factor and JPL occupancy correction may not transfer to a different hidden distribution.
The public prediction ensemble was selected on public time-ordered holdouts; hidden distribution shift may reduce its gain.
Prediction and internal planning use different model paths by design so that validated world-model and completion behavior is preserved.
The model cannot read hidden truth or future arrivals and may fail under distribution shift.
Historical analog days may not cover a materially different hidden arrival pattern.
